questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience a different country and a different culture as far away from Denmark as possible while still being able to understand the language. It was also crucial that the university was a good academic university.

questions.answer: To be honest, I do not recall how the registration proces was. As far as I recall it was fairly easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I believe all necessary information was available on the website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted, but I could have used more information on how registration works beforehand, as it was quite stressing scheduling classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Relax more regarding the registration. Look for the courses you might want, talk to people who know the courses to figure out if they are good, and do not be too concerned with waitlists. Usually people on waitlists get to enroll.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As stated above it was quite different. More quantity and less quality I would say.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are much more open, and you have to get used to superficial talks with strangers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are open. That people dare to take themselves serious. The way everything seems huge and more adventurous.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you just take a small step at a time in the end all the planning works out. Apply for I-House or a coop. Even though the coops look very shitty, they are actually very nice. 

Enrolling in courses is very different. You should prepare for not being settled on courses until the second, third or even fourth week, so it can be tough. Try the different courses, see what you like, talk to the professor about enrolment if you are unsure, and just try to enroll. Do not be afraid of waitlists. When the semester begins the waitlist goes very fast, and almost everyone end up with the courses they want.

If there is a course you would like to take, and you find a similar course in the computer science department, enroll in the one in the CS department.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the resources available online and reach out to the contact person at KU.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I have made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing academics and exploring the country.
